title: Spectral wake surge notes — autocorrelation & batching implications
content:
Quick context:
- Trying a different lens on bursts: instead of only looking at qps/time and p99s, I ran spectral (power spectral density) and autocorrelation on ingress timestamps for a set of production-like traces. Goal: find periodicities or long-memory effects that cause repeated warm-cache misses and batching inefficiencies ("wake" events).

Raw traces used:
- trace-A (weekday-peak, customer-sim): 10m, 600k requests
- trace-B (randomized poisson overlay): 15m, 1.1M requests
- trace-C (diurnal + microbursts): 30m, 2.4M requests

Method notes (quick):
- convert timestamps -> interarrival series (ms), resample to 10ms bins (0/1) to avoid jitter noise
- compute autocorrelation up to lag 2000 bins (~20s) using FFT-based conv (numpy.correlate-ish)
- apply Welch PSD (hann, 50% overlap) to binned series to look for frequency peaks in 0.01–2 Hz
- run on local laptop for exploratory, then small k8s job for full set (see linked PR)

Observations (high level):
- trace-A: strong low-frequency peak ~0.04 Hz (~25s period). Autocorr shows damped oscillations at same period up to ~8 cycles. Suggests a recurring influx — likely client-side batching/retries or a gateway doing fan-in flushes.
- trace-B: near-flat spectrum (expected). No significant autocorr beyond 200ms; behaves like Poisson.
- trace-C: broadband high-frequency energy 0.5–0.9 Hz plus low-frequency hump 0.03–0.05 Hz. The HF band corresponds to microbursts (~1–2s wide), LF is a ~20–30s envelope.

Why this matters for batching / latency:
- Our batching algorithm groups requests based on a short window (max-wait 8ms, dynamic) and a token budget. Periodic envelopes (20–30s) that repeatedly flood the worker cause frequent cold-ish prefixes for KV cache and short bursts that push batch sizes to max quickly, increasing p99s for mid-size requests.
- Microbursts (1–2s) create rapid throttle events and evictions in the hotpool: if eviction policy is LRU with small active set, we see cache churn exactly aligned with HF PSD band.

Small experiment summary (local probe with k=16 model replica):
- baseline (no spectral-aware changes): p50=22ms p95=130ms p99=460ms, CPU sched jitter visible
- add short prefix-caching heuristic (keep last 2 prefixes pinned for 30s): p50=20ms p95=110ms p99=320ms
- add spectral-aware delay (if energy in 0.4–1.0Hz band > threshold, increase max-wait by +4ms to allow coalescing HF bursts): p50=21ms p95=100ms p99=250ms
- combined heuristic (prefix pin + spectral delay): p50=19ms p95=95ms p99=210ms (best so far)

Raw micro-table from a run (100k requests sample window):
- Config | mean qps | p95 | p99 | avg batch size | cache-hit
- base   | 250      | 130 | 460 | 3.1            | 0.61
- pin2   | 245      | 110 | 320 | 3.4            | 0.72
- specD  | 240      | 100 | 250 | 3.9            | 0.69
- both   | 238      | 95  | 210 | 4.2            | 0.78

Notes on thresholds and false positives:
- PSD energy threshold chosen by histogram OOM: top 10% of energy windows flagged as HF-bursts. Needs tuning per-customer.
- Danger: delaying in a genuinely low-latency workload increases mean latency; must gate by SLA class (hosted free-tier vs enterprise).

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Is the LF (~25s) envelope originating from client SDK flush windows? Check SDKs for default flush timers ~25s. (ACTION: ask SDK owners Maya)
- Do certain tenant mixes amplify HF band because of synchronized background jobs? (ACTION: correlate tenant IDs with HF windows)
- Can a cheap exponential moving average (EMA) of PSD energy be computed online with <0.5% CPU overhead? If yes, could be used in edge proxies for early coalescing.

Next experiments to run (short checklist):
- [ ] Replay trace-C against a fleet with different cache eviction sizes (active set 128/256/512) and measure p99 delta
- [ ] Sweep spectral-delay + max-wait in grid: {+2,+4,+8}ms x {pin none, pin2, pin4} -> target: find knee where mean latency stops improving but p99 still drops
- [ ] Run tenant-level PSD to test if single-tenant sync patterns exist (privacy ok since using timestamps only)
- [ ] Implement quick streaming PSD estimator in Go (PR draft exists: linked_artifacts PR)

Implementation caveats:
- Need to ensure any "pin prefix" doesn't create memory blowups under large fanouts. Use soft-pinning with TTL and eviction weight.
- For spectral detector, avoid per-request FFTs. Use buffered counters per 10ms bin and run Welch every 5s on rolling window. This reduces cost and gives timely signal.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc as an evolving scratchpad — would like to convert to a short playbook if combined heuristics are robust across traces.
- If results hold, propose a small dedicated feature flag for tiered rollout: beta customers -> enterprise -> general.

References / quick links (copied):
- PSD primer: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welch%27s_method
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1189
- Correlate with telemetry: link to infra-bench slack thread above

End notes (timestamped):
- 2026-03-10 11:08 — consolidated combined run; p99 wins look encouraging but need more checks on tail noise due to VM steals
- 2026-03-10 16:35 — pushed small Go prototype for PSD estimator (local cpu ~0.3%)
